body:
`AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine` requires European exercise for `DoubleBarrier::KnockIn`, so a knock-in pays its cash at expiry. When the spot is already on or beyond a barrier, though, the engine returns the undiscounted cash, so the price jumps at the barrier (cash 10, barriers 80/120, r = 5%, 90 days):

| Spot | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 80.0001 | 9.87568 | 9.87568 |
| 80 | 10.00000 | 9.87578 |
| 79 | 10.00000 | 9.87578 |

The fixed value agrees with:
- `BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine`, which gives 9.875778 for the knocked-in option;
- the engine's own formula $D(T)\,\text{cash} - \text{KO}$, which tends to the discounted cash at the barriers;
- Haug's table in `testHaugValues`, where the 95/105 knock-in at 50% volatility is 9.8758.

The knocked-in rho is now $-t \cdot \text{value}$ instead of 0. KIKO and KOKI are unchanged: they have American exercise and pay at the hit, so the undiscounted cash is correct there.

**Tests:** the two degenerate knock-in rows in `testHaugValues` expected 10.0000; they weren't Haug values but matched the previous behaviour, and now expect 9.8758 ($10 e^{-0.05 \cdot 0.25}$). A new `testKnockedInValue` checks value and rho on and beyond both barriers, and continuity just inside them. Both fail on master and pass with this change.
title: Discount the cash of knocked-in double-barrier binary options
